answer: **Yes.** The excerpt has only one real character, Gregor Samsa, and he is drawn with notable depth for so short a passage. We see his shock ("Was ist mit mir geschehen?"), his melancholy at the rainy weather, and his wish to sleep on and forget the "Narrheiten," which hints at denial. His ingrained habits (sleeping on his right side) and his profession as a travelling salesman are mentioned, and his small personal touch of framing a magazine picture suggests an inner life and a backstory. The only other figure, the lady in the picture, is not an acting character but a detail that adds texture to Gregor's room and personality. No character feels inserted merely to satisfy a plot requirement.
